thread:
maya: heads up, running into intermittent 502s from model-serving pods when traffic goes through the interface endpoint in eu-west-1 :rotating_light:
ben: saw similar yesterday, thought it was a transient ALB sticky issue. any packet logs?
maya: dug into VPC flow logs + tcpdump from an affected node. saw lots of fragmentation and ICMP frag-needed messages. suspect MTU somewhere on the path (TGW or egress NAT).
jihoon: oh interesting. interface endpoints + TGW + NAT can shrink MTU unexpectedly. which subnet is the iface in and do you have an EIP proxy?
maya: iface in private subnet a, routed via TGW to central egress in shared services. NAT GW in shared account has an EIP and we also briefly had an ALB in front for healthchecks.
samir: can you paste the tcpdump snippet and the curl failure?
maya: sure — truncated:
```
16:02:11.123456 IP 10.64.3.22.443 > 10.64.8.11.54321: Flags [P.], seq 123:456, ack 789, win 64240, length 333
16:02:11.123457 ICMP 10.64.8.11 > 10.64.3.22: 3 Frag needed and DF set, mtu=1400
```
curl: (18) transfer closed with outstanding read data
```
ben: mtu=1400 is a red flag. our subnets are 9001 (GCE-style jumbo) internally but the TGW attachment to the shared account forces 1500/1400 sometimes depending on cross-account NAT.
ops-bot: noticed route-table change in shared-services account at 2026-03-10T21:01:02Z — TGW attachment re-associated to AZ-b.
jihoon: that re-association could have changed the egress path (and MTU) if the NAT stack is behind a proxy that does DF handling.
maya: tested from an affected pod with curl --max-time 10 -v and with smaller MSS it works: `curl --header "Host: model" --max-time 10 --ipv4 --path-as-is --no-keepalive --sslv3 --tcp-nodelay --mss=1360 https://private-model.local/health` returned 200
samir: ok that reproduces MTU problem. we need to find where DF/MTU negotiation is failing — could be ALB NLB proxy, TGW, or some transit firewall doing DF.
ben: quick checks:
- confirm SGs on iface endpoint allow ephemeral ports from ALB and NAT
- verify endpoint service has private DNS and correct hosted zone association
- check route tables for blackhole or an extra ENI hop
- check if any iptables MASQUERADE on shared NAT instances

jihoon: also check VPC endpoint ENI's source/destination check and proxy target. if S/D check is off and something sticky is in the middle, fragmentation may be dropped.
maya: ran these:
```
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters "Name=description,Values=*com.amazonaws.vpce*" --region eu-west-1
# confirmed ENIs in 3 AZs, S/D check=enabled
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters "Name=route.tgw-attachment,Values=tgw-attach-0123"
# routes propogated to private subnets
```
maya: SGs looked fine. but I saw a pair of rules on the shared NAT ENI that force DF packet reassessments (policy managed by older firewall appliance). we also have an ALB healthcheck path hitting the iface which might be causing path MTU discovery to get asymmetric replies.
ops-bot: incident-tag: p1-network-frag, owner=maya, sla=72h
ben: quick mitigation — enable prefix/KV caching or route via alternate egress (bypass shared NAT) for the affected model-serving ASG. toggle route table to point to a NAT in same account that preserves jumbo frames.
maya: can do a targeted route override for the model-serving subnets to route via local NAT (will require a short maintenance window). who needs to approve?
samir: I'll approve for a 15-min window. schedule now?
jihoon: before that, can we try reducing MSS on the ALB/NLB target groups? sometimes the LB rewrites DF bits and causes fragmentation.
ben: NLB is L4 so less likely; ALB could. but we only have ALB for healthchecks, traffic is through iface endpoint which is an ENI target.
maya: starting a canary change: add route table association swap to local-nat-rt for the two affected private subnets. will do 1 AZ at a time and monitor 5 min.
infra-bot: starting runbook step: update route-table rtb-0a1b2c for subnet-0c -> associate with route table rtb-localnat, user=maya
maya: swap scheduled, rolling now. will post metrics and tcpdump after AZ1 flip.
(some minutes later)
maya: AZ1 swapped. no 502s in the next 6 min, tcpdump no ICMP frag-needed.
samir: nice. keep AZ2 for later after we confirm stability. :thumbsup:
ben: follow-up — we should push a long-term fix: replace firewall appliance or fix DF handling, and add a healthcheck that validates MTU path (simple large payload request). also add a probe that checks for ICMP frag-needed in flow logs.
jihoon: agree. I'll add an automation ticket to the infra backlog to add a path-MTU monitor and a runbook for interface-endpoint MTU problems.
maya: filing postmortem and linking in this thread. thanks all.
ops-bot: closed runbook step, status=success, duration=420s
